simple.meaning: פָּגַר (pâgar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to relax , i.e. become exhausted.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in 1 Samuel, beginning at 1 Samuel 30:10. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פָּגַר (H6296) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פָּגַר (pâgar) / H6296 is traced through 1 Samuel 30:10, 1 Samuel 30:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6296. pagar [ מָּגַר ] verb Pi`el be exhausted, faint ( מְּגַר ᵑ7 derived species tear down, destroy ; Assyrian pagru, body, corpse; Late Hebrew מֶּגֶר = Biblical Hebrew; Aramaic מַּגְרָא , ; Palmyrene פגר ; Mandean פאגרא Nö M § 89 ); — Perfect 3plural מִן מִּגְּרוּ they were too faint to go, etc. 1Sam 30:10 , 21 .

occurrences.englishText: But David pursued, he and four hundred men; for two hundred stayed behind, who were so faint that they couldn’t go over the brook Besor.

David came to the two hundred men, who were so faint that they could not follow David, whom also they had made to stay at the brook Besor; and they went out to meet David, and to meet the people who were with him. When David came near to the people, he greeted them.
